title: State transitions for minimum climbing cost
summary: Each state takes the smaller cumulative minimum cost of its two predecessors and adds cost[i], the cost of the current step.
context: Each move climbs 1 or 2 steps, cost[i] is the nonnegative cost paid upon landing on step i, and starting on the ground is free. Let dp[i] denote the minimum cumulative cost to reach step i.
description: Green blocks dp[1] through dp[9] run horizontally from left to right; odd-indexed cost labels sit above and even-indexed ones sit below, pointing into their respective dp blocks. States dp[1] and dp[2] receive only their own cost arrows; starting at dp[3], brackets and min markers combine the two preceding states into the next state, with a plus sign beside the incoming cost arrow for paying the current step's cost. Below the diagram appear the initial states and general recurrence dp[i] = min(dp[i - 1], dp[i - 2]) + cost[i] without concrete cost numbers.

The final move onto step i must come from either step i - 1 or step i - 2. Because landing on step i pays cost[i] regardless of predecessor, compare predecessor costs dp[i - 1] and dp[i - 2] to pick the smaller cumulative cost and then add cost[i].

From the ground one can step directly onto step 1 or step 2, giving dp[1] = cost[1]. Because cost[1] is nonnegative, passing through step 1 on the way to step 2 can never cost less than stepping straight onto step 2, so dp[2] = cost[2]. The table below lists steps 1 through 9 individually for lookup; the "Ground" origin and "no worse than via step 1" notes are supplied from the problem rules rather than a separate ground node drawn in the figure.
